name: Six-Concept Layer-Union Collision
definition: In the four-cube with integer word convention $x=\sum_{i=0}^3x_i2^i$, take $X=\{0,1,2,3,7,8\}$. Its graph is a square with two pendant edges.
parameters: $X$ has six concepts, isometric dimension four, VC dimension two, and signed minimal nonfaces $(12,12),(10,10),(9,9),(6,4),(5,4)$.
properties: $X$ is ample and corner-peelable. Its balanced coordinates are 0 and 1. Each singleton is a successful layer set, but their union fails recovery: the four relevant fibres collapse to two repeated singletons, $T_9=T_{10}=\{8\}$ and $T_5=T_6=\{4\}$. Thus successful layer sets are not union-closed for arbitrary ample families.
